system_description.narrative_title: US–Iran conflict de‑escalation signals and oil‑market response
system_description.narrative_summary: The dominant narrative is that tentative diplomatic outreach and public US restraint are producing signs of de‑escalation in the US–Iran confrontation, which in turn is driving rapid reactions in energy markets and allied military posture. As an open system, diplomatic signals, military incidents (Houthi strikes, pipeline hits, evacuations), political decisions, and market expectations continually feed back on one another, producing volatile but easing oil prices while leaving the region sensitive to new shocks. Ongoing attacks, sanctions actions and domestic politics create persistent nonlinearities and short‑term reversal risks despite the current downward pressure on energy risk premia.
system_description.scope: Inside: US–Iran military and diplomatic interactions; Gulf states' military actions and coalition moves; Houthi and asymmetric attacks on shipping and infrastructure; global oil and gas market responses; allied military posture (base evacuations, command HQ); sanctions and diplomatic initiatives.
system_description.super_system: Global geopolitical–energy security system (international politics, major‑power diplomacy, and global energy markets).
adjacent_subsystems: Gulf regional security architecture & military coalitions
Maritime shipping & chokepoint (Strait of Hormuz) security
Domestic politics in the US, UK, and Gulf states
evidence_headlines: Trump tells Reuters that Qatar, Saudi Arabia want peaceful Iran deal, US ready for strikes if needed
Oil falls below $90 as Trump downplays prospect of escalation with Iran
US removes planes from second UK military base after Iran threat
Saudi East-West oil pipeline hit in Medina region, state media reports
Qatari PM makes unscheduled stop at G7 to brief Europeans post Trump talks
Vance Reaches Out to Iranian Hard-Liner in Bid to Restart Peace Talks

variables.name: Diplomatic engagement level
variables.description: Measures the intensity and frequency of formal and informal diplomatic contacts, outreach, and back‑channel communications between conflict actors and mediators.

variables.name: Military conflict intensity
variables.description: Captures the severity and tempo of kinetic military exchanges, strikes, and direct combat operations across the theatre.

variables.name: Asymmetric attack rate
variables.description: The rate of irregular or proxy attacks (e.g., missile, drone, sabotage) against ships, oil facilities, and other soft targets over time.

variables.name: Military posture readiness
variables.description: Level of force deployment, alert status, relocations, evacuations, and command posture maintained by external and regional forces.

variables.name: Energy market risk premium
variables.description: The geopolitical risk component added to energy prices reflecting market compensation for potential supply disruptions and uncertainty.

variables.name: Crude price level
variables.description: The prevailing market price level for benchmark crude oil products (spot and near‑term futures) in real terms.

variables.name: Oil production capacity
variables.description: Available regional oil extraction and export capability measured as working output capacity relative to baseline.

variables.name: Shipping disruption severity
variables.description: Degree of interruptions to maritime transit including route closures, interdictions, and navigational hazards affecting throughput.

variables.name: Energy infrastructure damage level
variables.description: Cumulative physical damage to pipelines, terminals, storage, and processing facilities expressed as lost functional capacity.

variables.name: Sanctions pressure level
variables.description: Intensity and breadth of economic, financial, and trade restrictions applied against actors in the dispute and their networks.

variables.name: Domestic political pressure for escalation
variables.description: Aggregate domestic political and public pressure pushing policymakers toward more aggressive or restrained responses.

variables.name: Negotiation momentum
variables.description: Directional speed and strength of progress or regression in diplomatic negotiations and confidence‑building processes.

variables.name: Market expectations of conflict trajectory
variables.description: Markets' collective expectation about the future path of escalation versus de‑escalation, reflected in forward contracts and derivatives pricing.

variables.name: Global oil demand trend
variables.description: Underlying trend in worldwide oil consumption driven by economic activity, seasonal patterns, and structural demand shifts.

variables.name: Shipping cost level
variables.description: Average freight, insurance, and rerouting costs for maritime oil and gas transport across relevant sea lanes.

variables.name: Allied coalition coherence
variables.description: Degree of alignment, information‑sharing, and coordinated military/diplomatic action among external partner groups.

catalysts.title: Trump meets Qatar prime minister
catalysts.description: Planned meeting between Trump and Qatar's PM to discuss Iran diplomacy, likely shaping de‑escalation messaging and coordination with Gulf states.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: 'Trump to meet Qatar's prime minister'; also 'Trump tells Reuters that Qatar, Saudi Arabia want peaceful Iran deal.'

catalysts.title: Vance back‑channel outreach to Iranian hard‑liner
catalysts.description: US negotiator Vance's contact with an Iranian hard‑liner to restart talks could open low‑visibility diplomacy and test confidence‑building steps.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: 'Vance Reaches Out to Iranian Hard‑Liner' and 'Vance Considers Direct Talks With Iran Hard‑Liner'.

catalysts.title: Risk of renewed short, intense US strikes
catalysts.description: Political and military signals leave a non‑zero chance of short, focused US strikes or limited kinetic renewals despite public restraint.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'U.S. Warns Gulf of Possible Short, Intense Renewal of Iran War After Midterms'; 'US ready for strikes if needed' and evacuation reports.

catalysts.title: Continued Houthi missile/drone attacks
catalysts.description: Ongoing Houthi strikes and interceptions in the Gulf and attacks on Saudi infrastructure and shipping navigation systems continue to drive instability.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Saudi-led coalition reports Houthi missile, drone interceptions'; 'Saudi East‑West oil pipeline hit'; 'Iran attacks shipping navigation systems...'.

catalysts.title: OPEC+/Saudi output near prewar levels
catalysts.description: Reports that Saudi and OPEC+ production have rebounded near prewar rates will ease supply tightness and influence prices and risk premia.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Saudi oil production rebounds close to prewar levels'; 'OPEC’s Oil Production Nears Prewar Levels...'.

catalysts.title: Adnoc evaluates Strait‑bypass logistics
catalysts.description: ADNOC's assessment of options to bypass the Strait of Hormuz could shift shipping patterns and reduce chokepoint vulnerability if implemented.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: 'Adnoc Gas Still Evaluating Options to Bypass Strait of Hormuz'.

catalysts.title: US aircraft/base evacuations and relocations
catalysts.description: Evacuations and relocation of US aircraft and officials from allied bases signal changes in force posture and allied burden‑sharing debates.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'U.S. Aircraft Evacuated From Second U.K. Base'; 'US removes planes from second UK military base after Iran threat.'

catalysts.title: Continuation and expansion of allied sanctions
catalysts.description: Ongoing diplomatic pressure and fresh sanctions by partners could raise economic costs on Iran and shape negotiation incentives.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Canada reimposes sanctions on 11 Iranian entities'; 'Rubio says US will keep imposing "devastating" costs on Iran.'
